about: Golden vectors for canonicalization and hashing of Ductus evidence v2 (DAN-127). All data is invented.
The file is ASCII: every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape. Read it with a JSON parser from the file bytes, not through a bundler import, which may rewrite keys such as __proto__.

The expected values were derived outside the repository (RFC texts, hand-written canonical strings, an independent implementation). Never regenerate them from the code under test: a change that alters any value is a change of the evidence contract.

definitions.canonicalBytes: UTF-8 encoding of the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of a JSON value. No Unicode normalization. A lone surrogate or a non-finite number has no canonical form.
definitions.documentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the canonical document JSON.
definitions.segmentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an evidence segment v2. The server hashes the bytes it received and accepts them only when they are the canonical bytes of a valid segment.
definitions.chain: predecessorSegmentHash is the segmentHash of the segment accepted before it, null for the first. The head is the last segmentHash together with the number of segments.
definitions.segmentTime: observedStartedAt and observedEndedAt are whole minutes in UTC, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:00.000Z. An event has no time; events are ordered by sequence.
definitions.eventSource: One of editor, paste, cut, drop, composition, system-replacement, keyless-input and unattributed; no other value and no default. editor is written only for a change positively attributed to typing in the editor. composition is written only when the capture layer has positive proof that the character was composed with physical keys; in every other case, also when there is no proof or the proof is ambiguous, keyless-input is written. keyless-input is text entered without key events (dictation, an on-screen keyboard, an input method with no such proof). unattributed is every change with no positive attribution, and a paste or a drop whose event cannot be relied on. The server cannot check these rules; the capture layer keeps them.
definitions.receiptDigest: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1 (payloadDigestSha256).
definitions.receiptSignatureV1: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1; raw 64-byte signature, base64url without padding. Decision D-92 replaces this for receipt v2.
definitions.receiptDigestV2: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v2 (payloadDigestSha256). D below is its 32 raw bytes.
definitions.receiptSignatureV2: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the 59 bytes UTF-8(ductus-evidence-receipt-v2) || 0x0a || D (decision D-92); raw 64-byte signature, base64url without padding. Never over the canonical bytes of the payload and never over D alone.
definitions.evidenceDomainId: The identifier of an evidence domain (one institution in one region) in the signed receipt v2: a canonical lowercase version 4 UUID of 36 characters. Random, opaque and immutable; never derived from the id or the name of an institution, from a region or from a time.

chain.note: Two chained segments from the empty document to a signed receipt for each. Documents are canonical documents (schemaVersion 1) of two paragraphs with invented UUID v4 ids. Steps are in the closed format ductus-edit-steps-v1: each one inserts one text node at a ProseMirror position (UTF-16), with no marks. Receipts are signed with the Ed25519 test key published as TEST 1 in RFC 8032 section 7.1; only its public half is stored here. signingSeedSha256 is the SHA-256 of the 32 private bytes printed in the RFC, so that a test can show those bytes are in none of the vector files.

segmentPayloads.note: Byte edits of chain.segments[base].canonicalUtf8Hex that must not be accepted. find/replace are UTF-8 text, findHex/replaceHex are bytes; find occurs exactly once. recanonicalizesToBase: the edited bytes parse to the same segment, so only the bytes are wrong. canonicalReplace: JCS writes the parsed edit as the base with find replaced by canonicalReplace, so the edited bytes differ from their own canonical form exactly there. canonicalJcs: the edited bytes are canonical JCS, so the segment validator is what rejects them.

eventTime.note: Owner decision of 10 October 2026 (D-24, D-56): a segment carries no time per event and no time finer than a minute, and the server refuses a segment that does; it never rounds one. formerSegments are the two chain segments of the first revision of this file (DAN-127), byte for byte: canonical JCS that was valid then and must be refused now, because its events carry occurredAt and elapsedMs and its observed times carry seconds. formerSegmentHash is the hash that revision published for them. The edits with the classes event-time, time-precision, time-form and closed-shape under segmentPayloads.rejected, and time-in-capture-context, each break one rule on the current first segment.

stepFormat.note: DAN-183 (Z10): a segment carries only steps of the closed format ductus-edit-steps-v1. formerSegments are the two chain segments of this file before DAN-183b, byte for byte: canonical JCS whose captureContext names the invented test format ductus-test-insert-text-v0 and whose steps are insert-text at an offset of one node. formerSegmentHash is the hash the file published for them.

sizeLimit.note: Set the text of the one text node inserted by events[0].steps[0] of segmentWithoutPadding (steps[0].slice.content[0].text) to padding.unit repeated padding.count times. The unit is two UTF-8 bytes and one UTF-16 code unit, so the limit is seen to count bytes. The document hashes in the segment are those of the padded document. overLimit appends extraText to that text.

receiptV2.note: Receipt v2 (D-92, DAN-54). The signed payload carries revision, clientTransactionId, evidenceDomainId and principalId next to the fields of receipt v1. The signature is Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over signingInputHex: the 26 bytes of the text ductus-evidence-receipt-v2, one line feed (0x0a) and the 32 raw bytes of payloadDigestSha256, 59 bytes in all. accepted[0] is the contract vector of docs/BACKEND.md section 4.1, with the fields in the order of RFC 8785: clientTransactionId after acceptedAt, evidenceDomainId between eventCount and evidencePackageId, principalId between previousReceiptId and receiptId, revision after receiptSchema. Signatures are made with the key chain.verificationKey. The evidence domain ids and the principal ids are random version 4 UUIDs drawn for this file; they name no institution and no person. revision and clientTransactionId mean the commit in which the segment of the receipt was accepted (owner decision of 11 October 2026, issue 87 comment 6105502093, point 5). A revision may have more than one receipt, and the sequence numbers of a segment say nothing about the revision: accepted[0] is the first receipt of its package and carries revision 7. principalId is the author the server took from the session of the request that sent the segment, never a value the client wrote. acceptedAt is the start of the UTC minute in which the server accepted the segment, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:00.000Z; every other form is refused and none is rounded (issue 87 comment 6107934097, point 2). A receipt v2 states three things: the bytes with segmentHash were received and stored, they continue the chain after predecessorSegmentHash, and the document whose hash is the finalDocumentHash of that segment was saved as revision. rejectedPayloads change accepted[0].payload: set replaces or adds fields, remove deletes them. The class acceptance-fields holds one change for each rule of the fields a receipt v2 shares with a receipt v1. The class accepted-at-minute holds instants a receipt v1 may carry and a receipt v2 may not. The class principal-id holds the author left out and in every form it may not have. rejectedSignatures are valid signatures of the same key over messageHex, which is not the signing input of accepted[0]. keyEntry is what the entry of the trusted key list for chain.verificationKey holds next to the key itself: it belongs to evidenceDomainId with the purpose receipt, is active (validTo null) and was never revoked. rejectedKeys change that entry: under each changed entry the unchanged accepted[0], whose signature is valid, is refused with reason. acceptedKeys change it too, and under each of them accepted[0] still verifies. validFrom and validTo of a key are whole UTC minutes in the form of acceptedAt, and a retired key that was never revoked vouches for a receipt with acceptedAt < validTo (owner decision of 11 October 2026, issue 87 comment 6108490197): an entry whose validFrom or validTo has any other form is no key (key_unknown) and is never rounded, so a key that ends inside a minute is refused as a key and no receipt is judged by it. Nor is an entry a key unless validFrom < validTo.

ed25519Points.note: Encodings of points of edwards25519 (RFC 8032, 5.1.3) for a verifier that judges a public key and the R of a signature by their bytes. accepted are canonical encodings of points of the prime-order subgroup: multiples of the base point and the public key of chain.verificationKey. rejected hold four classes. small-order: the eight points whose order divides 8, found as [L]Q for points Q. mixed-order: points on the curve outside the prime-order subgroup, namely the public key of chain.verificationKey plus each small-order point but the identity, and the points with y = 3 and y = 4. not-on-curve: a y below p for which x^2 = (y^2 - 1)/(d y^2 + 1) has no root. non-canonical: a y at or above p = 2^255 - 19, or the sign of x set where x is 0. No point of the prime-order subgroup has y below 19, so none has a second spelling. mixedOrderSignature is a signature over receiptV2.accepted[0].signingInputHex for which [S]B = R + [h]A holds with A the mixed-order key pointHex and h = SHA-512(R || A || M), both as it is and reduced modulo L: the nonce was picked so that h is a multiple of 8. A runtime that checks that equation and does not refuse the key verifies it; a runtime that multiplies both sides by 8 verifies every signature made with that scalar. All values were derived by arithmetic outside this repository.

sequenceRanges.note: Ranges of sequence numbers with the number of events they are said to hold, for every validator that reads sequenceFrom, sequenceTo and a count together: the ingest descriptor, the segment (where the count is the number of its events) and both receipts. A range holds sequenceTo - sequenceFrom + 1 events. The rejected ranges named rounding pass a check written sequenceFrom + eventCount - 1 = sequenceTo in IEEE 754 doubles, where the sum rounds to an even number. The rejected ranges empty-range, empty-range-above-one and negative-count agree with sequenceTo - sequenceFrom = eventCount - 1 and hold no event: a range holds at least one event and never ends before it starts, whatever the count says.

rejected.name: rounding-two-events-at-largest-number
rejected.note: One sequence number, the largest safe integer, and two events.

rejected.name: rounding-three-events-in-last-two-numbers
rejected.note: Two sequence numbers and three events.

rejected.name: rounding-largest-count-from-2
rejected.note: The range from 2 holds one event fewer than the largest safe integer.

rejected.name: end-above-safe-integer
rejected.note: 2^53 as the end: not exact in a double, though the count agrees with it.

rejected.name: count-above-range
rejected.note: Two events in a range of one sequence number.

rejected.name: count-below-range
rejected.note: Two events in a range of three sequence numbers.

rejected.name: count-one-below-largest-range
rejected.note: One event too few for the whole range.

rejected.name: end-before-start
rejected.note: The range ends before it starts.

rejected.name: empty-range
rejected.note: No event: the end is one below the start, which agrees with a count of 0.

rejected.name: start-at-zero
rejected.note: Sequence numbers start at 1.

rejected.name: empty-range-above-one
rejected.note: No event, with both ends valid numbers on their own: the count agrees with the range, so only the rules that a range holds an event and does not end before it starts refuse it.

rejected.name: negative-count
rejected.note: The end two below the start agrees with a count of -1.

rejected.name: no-event-in-one-number
rejected.note: A range of one sequence number said to hold no event.
